title: Reformed map: two kinds—lighter compatible with holiness; graver death-liable until repentance
source_text: XXIII. Ex quibus omnibus evidenter constat Doctores Scholae Reformatae duo peccatorum genera, ut diximus, agnoscere. Unum leviorum quae simul stare possunt cum bona conscientia, & puritate illa cordis, sine qua nemo videbit Dominum, & quae proinde personam fidelem in qua reperiuntur aeternae damnationi actu obnoxiam non reddunt, & ineptam quae in regnum coelorum ingrediatur; etiamsi in aliquo ejusmodi peccato a morte deprehendatur: Alterum vero graviorum, in quae lapsus aliquis, & antequam ex iis per poenitentiam resurget, servare non potest bonam conscientiam, & cordis munditiem necessariam ad Deum videndum: sed per ea fit actu mortis aeternae reus, eaque obnoxius, & ineptus ut in regnum coelorum admittatur, adeo ut, si mors illum in eo statu opprimeret, in aeternum damnandus esset, & a gloria coelesti excludendus.
pass_a_gloss: From all which it is evidently established that the doctors of the Reformed school acknowledge two kinds of sins, as we have said. One of lighter sins which can stand together with a good conscience and that purity of heart without which no one will see the Lord, and which therefore do not render the faithful person in whom they are found actually liable to eternal damnation, and unfit to enter the kingdom of heaven; even if he is overtaken by death in some such sin: But the other of graver sins, into which when someone has fallen, and before he rises from them by repentance, he cannot keep a good conscience and the cleanness of heart necessary for seeing God: but by them he becomes actually guilty of eternal death, and liable thereto, and unfit to be admitted into the kingdom of heaven, so that if death should oppress him in that state he would be eternally damned and excluded from heavenly glory.
pass_b_english: Reformed doctors thus own two kinds: lighter faults compatible with holiness even at death.
Graver falls, until repentance, make one actually death-liable and unfit for heaven.

choices.why: Present liability, not mere remote possibility.
